Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 | The optimized audit-log path applies math.floor/ceil to datetime values, so authorized callers using optimized_pagination=true receive a server error once rows exist. | api-contract | 0.99 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug. Looking at the diff, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 uses math.floor/math.ceil on the value obtained via getattr(item, self.key). When used with audit logs ordered by '-datetime', the key would be a datetime field. Applying math.floor() or math.ceil() to a datetime object will raise a TypeError since datetime objects don't support these mathematical operations. The DateTimePaginator (the original paginator) handles datetime values differently, but this new OptimizedCursorPaginator doesn't account for datetime types, causing a server error when optimized_pagination=true is used with actual audit log data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 | Django QuerySets reject negative slice indexes, so every advanced request with a negative cursor offset raises ValueError instead of providing the advertised reverse pagination. | correctness | 0.99 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In the OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() method at lines 879-882, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code attempts to use negative slicing: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` where start_offset is negative. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and will raise an AssertionError or ValueError. The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' but this is false - Django explicitly rejects negative slice indices. This is a real correctness bug that would cause the 'advanced pagination' feature to fail with an exception.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a type mismatch. Looking at the diff, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 838 uses math.floor/math.ceil on the value, treating it as numeric. However, in organization_auditlogs.py, this paginator is used with order_by='-datetime', meaning the key would be a datetime field. The DateTimePaginator (which was previously used) has special handling for datetime values, but OptimizedCursorPaginator does not - it assumes numeric values. This would cause errors when trying to apply math.floor/math.ceil to datetime objects.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that OptimizedCursorPaginator (lines 818-912) duplicates nearly all the logic from BasePaginator.get_result() method, with only minor variations in offset handling. Looking at the diff, the new class copies the entire get_result implementation including cursor handling, queryset building, hit counting, result processing, and cursor building - all of which already exist in BasePaginator. The only meaningful difference is the negative offset handling in lines 875-884. This is a legitimate maintainability concern: if bugs are fixed in BasePaginator.get_result(), they would need to be manually propagated to OptimizedCursorPaginator. This is a real architectural/scope concern grounded in the specific code added by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 | No authorized optimized-pagination integration test exercises datetime audit rows, so the math.floor(datetime) crash in the new paginator is undetected. | testing | 0.99 |

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at line 840 in the diff, the OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key method does `math.floor(value)` or `math.ceil(value)` on the attribute retrieved via `getattr(item, self.key)`. When used with audit logs ordered by '-datetime', the key would be 'datetime' and the value would be a datetime object. Calling math.floor() on a datetime object will raise a TypeError since datetime objects don't support the __floor__ method. This is a genuine bug that would crash when the OptimizedCursorPaginator is used with datetime-based ordering, which is exactly how it's configured in the audit logs endpoint (order_by='-datetime').
